prompt: **In recent years, there has been growing interest in the relationship between equality and personal achievement. Some people believe that individuals can achieve more in egalitarian societies. Others believe that high levels of personal achievement are possible only if individuals are free to succeed or fail according to their individual merits. Discuss both sides and give your own opinion.**
essay:
Whether individuals should be given equal opportunities or rewarded according to their merits has become a topic of debate. While some people believe that society should provide similar opportunities to everyone, others argue that individuals should be rewarded according to their abilities and achievements. In my opinion, both principles are important because society needs to ensure equality of opportunity while also recognising individual effort and talent.

On the one hand, everyone should have access to basic opportunities regardless of their social or financial background. This includes equal access to education, healthcare and employment opportunities. Such an approach can particularly benefit people from disadvantaged backgrounds, who may otherwise struggle to reach their full potential. For instance, scholarships and financial assistance can allow talented students from low-income families to receive a quality education and develop successful careers. In this way, equality of opportunity can promote social mobility and reduce discrimination.

On the other hand, competition and rewards can motivate people to achieve more. When individuals know that their effort, talent and achievements will be recognised, they are more likely to work hard and pursue ambitious goals. For example, if employees receive promotions based on their performance, highly productive workers are likely to remain motivated because their additional effort can lead to career advancement. In contrast, if everyone receives the same rewards regardless of their contribution, some people may lose the incentive to excel. Therefore, recognising individual merit can encourage productivity, innovation and personal achievement.

In my opinion, both equality and merit are essential for a successful society. Equality should mean equal opportunities rather than identical outcomes. Governments should therefore adopt a balanced approach by ensuring that everyone has a fair starting point while also creating systems that reward individuals according to their abilities and efforts. This can promote both social fairness and economic development.

In conclusion, although equal opportunities are necessary to ensure fairness and social mobility, individual merit should also be recognised and rewarded. A society that combines these two principles can give people a fair chance to succeed while encouraging them to achieve their full potential.
